pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item() labels non-normal; 'AC-2' test asserts exact li text for high, low, normal.
WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id; 'AC-3' test covers high (ids 1,3 order), low, normal.
Unfiltered query ORDER BY id; 'AC-4' test asserts order of all items.
nav() renders four filters with current as <strong>; 'AC-5' asserts exact nav for all four views.
Invalid or empty priority returns 400 before any query; 'AC-6' test covers High, urgent, empty, __proto__ and checks no <li>.
Empty message logic in src/index.js; 'AC-7' test checks the no-match messages and 'No items yet.' in all four views with the table emptied.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; 'AC-8' test asserts it. The check script was updated to accept queries and has tests.

findings.what: README mentions the filter but not the 400 for other values or the '— high/low' labels.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the 400 response and the labels.

lenses.note: Spec exists with go and dated decisions; the change follows them and adds nothing beyond the ask. The traffic-check relaxation is needed by AC-8.
All 8 items are met. Every States row has a test in the 'states' describe block. The spec was not edited after the go.
Tests assert exact output and would fail on regression. The traffic.test.js fake-app change is justified and nothing was weakened. I did not run the suite; CI runs it.
README updated, with a minor gap on the 400 and the labels.
Handles an empty value, __proto__ and a parameterised query. Distinguishing 'no match' from an empty table costs one extra COUNT query, which is acceptable.
Priority is whitelisted and bound as a parameter, and titles are still HTML-escaped; no injection found. The route regex still refuses spaces and #.
The diff adds only a simple server-rendered nav in src/index.js, with no UI or style files.
